topic: OpenAI rates GPT-6.2 Astra its first released model at 'High' for AI self-improvement
announced_at: 17 November 2026 (OpenAI launch post and GPT-6.2 system card)
why_selected: Replaces the held California v OpenAI package. It is the highest-scoring eligible story, and every claim in the script traces to a primary source: OpenAI's own system card and launch post, and Vals AI's own post. It is more original than a routine launch video because it reads the system card rather than the benchmarks, and it gives an independent counterpoint. The 'Critical cybersecurity' rating was deliberately left out because it is not new.
disclosure: Disclosure: I'm built by Anthropic, an OpenAI competitor whose IPO is in today's candidates. Epoch AI's evaluation of GPT-6.2 Astra compares it favourably with Anthropic models; that comparison is deliberately kept out of the script. The script relies on OpenAI's own documents and one independent tester.
research_summary: On 17 November 2026 OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol. In the accompanying system card, OpenAI says Astra is the first model it has deployed externally that meets the 'High' threshold for AI self-improvement in its Preparedness Framework. OpenAI's launch post explains that this means the model's impact equals giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, relative to 2024. The card calls the threshold an early milestone ahead of fully automated, recursive self-improvement, which Astra does not reach. Independent tester Vals AI measured an incremental gain on its AI-research index, from 27.07% to 29.01%, and judged full automation of AI research unlikely. The rating is OpenAI's own assessment.

key_facts: System card: Astra is the first externally deployed OpenAI model at 'High' for AI self-improvement; Sol is below it.
OpenAI's meaning of High: like giving every OpenAI researcher an extra, highly capable research engineer, relative to 2024.
OpenAI calls it an early milestone ahead of fully automated, recursive self-improvement.
Vals AI: 29.01% on its RSI-Index vs 27.07% for GPT-6 Astra, an incremental gain; full automation of AI research unlikely.
uncertainties: The High rating is OpenAI's own assessment of its own model, not an independent measurement.
The assessment rests on five research-engineering evaluations; reports say Astra missed some of OpenAI's own stated cutoffs (secondary sources only; not in the script).
Epoch AI's results are mixed and one widely shared summary overstates them; the script uses Vals instead.
OpenAI's pages were read through their indexed text; openai.com and deploymentsafety.openai.com cannot be opened from this environment.
context: AI that helps build better AI is the scenario safety frameworks were written for. OpenAI's framework has two levels: High, which this model reaches, and Critical, meaning fully automated self-improvement, which it does not. Early reviews of the model's everyday use were rough, which is a separate question from this rating.
script:
OpenAI ka naya AI, AI banane mein madad karne laga hai. OpenAI khud keh raha hai.

Naye GPT-6.2 Astra ke system card mein OpenAI ne likha: yeh pehla public model hai jo 'AI self-improvement' mein unke High level tak pahuncha.

Matlab, OpenAI ke hisaab se: har researcher ke saath ek extra research engineer.

Lekin independent tester Vals AI ko pichle model se sirf thoda sudhaar dikha.

OpenAI ise bas 'early milestone' kehta hai. AI khud ko upgrade nahi kar raha, par agla AI banane mein uska haath badh raha hai.

factcheck.story: OpenAI rates GPT-6.2 Astra its first released model at 'High' for AI self-improvement

claims.text: GPT-6.2 Astra was released on 17 November 2026
OpenAI's system card says GPT-6.2 Astra is 'the first model we are deploying externally that meets the High threshold for AI Self-Improvement'
claims.note: The same sentence appeared in OpenAI's indexed card text in two separate searches. The script paraphrases it in Hinglish rather than quoting. The rating is OpenAI's own assessment.

claims.text: OpenAI: a 'High' designation means the model's impact is 'equivalent to giving every OpenAI researcher an additional, highly capable research engineer as an assistant, relative to their 2024 baseline'
claims.note: Wording from OpenAI's launch post as indexed. Matches the April 2025 Preparedness Framework definition. The card's 17 Nov change log mentions wording updates to the threat-modelling section; the launch-post definition is the current one.

claims.text: Vals AI's pre-release testing: GPT-6.2 Astra scored 29.01% on its RSI-Index, 'an incremental gain over 27.07% for GPT-6 Astra'
claims.note: Vals' own post. It also calls Astra the highest-scoring OpenAI model it has tested and says full automation of AI research is unlikely. Vals' RSI leaderboard: https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/rsi_index

claims.text: OpenAI's card calls the High threshold 'an early milestone for preparing safeguards ahead of models capable of fully automated, recursive self improvement'
claims.note: Supports the script's 'AI khud ko upgrade nahi kar raha'. Vals also judged full automation of AI research unlikely.

claims.text: No earlier OpenAI model it released met the High threshold for AI self-improvement (GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna and GPT-5.6 are below it)
claims.note: Basis for the closing line 'agla AI banane mein uska haath badh raha hai', which is an editorial reading of OpenAI's rating, not a measured fact.

claims.text: GPT-6.2 Astra is available to paid ChatGPT plans in ChatGPT Work and Codex, and in the API at $8/$40 per million tokens (20% below GPT-6 Astra)
claims.note: Not in the script. Rollout is gradual; not available in regular Chat.

claims.text: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol meet OpenAI's Critical cybersecurity threshold
claims.note: Not used: GPT-6 Astra was already rated Critical for cyber, so presenting it as new would mislead.

claims.text: Epoch AI found no meaningful improvement over GPT-6 Astra
claims.note: Epoch's own write-up (https://epoch.ai/publications/how-good-are-fable-5-2-and-gpt-6-2-astra-at-real-work) reports gains on several tasks and weaknesses on open-ended research, so this summary overstates it. Not used.
